data.title: The Kitchen Calendar
data.text: At No. 14 Church Lane, the kitchen calendar was left behind when you broke the house. Ruth Vey ran her home by a calendar in four colours of pen; green meant good news. Dorothy Pell lived next door. She told the wardens she had voted against the 2017 flood levy because she did not want anyone wondering, and she still came to every drill and knocked on every door on her list. You broke both houses, then Riverside dam. St Bride's, the church on the hill, remained intact. A notice on its door said the church hall would stay open as a place to rest until the last train left. It promised tea and biscuits. The river ran greyer beneath a light haze.
